scenario.description: A plant safety officer must decide whether to reopen a battery-charging room after a smoke alarm and finalize the room's repair, ventilation, monitoring, and charging plan, with input from facilities engineering, production supervision, and environmental compliance.

shared_context.S1: The battery-charging room was closed after its smoke alarm sounded during the afternoon charging cycle.
shared_context.S2: The room is needed for the next production shift's battery charging, and the visible smoke has cleared.
shared_context.S3: Elena, the plant safety officer, has authority to decide whether the room can reopen and under what conditions.
shared_context.S4: The plant's incident-response routine requires Elena to call on facilities, production supervision, and environmental compliance in that order; each representative reports findings and required controls, after which Elena records the controls and issues the reopening decision.
shared_context.S5: Plant procedure requires each representative to formally document and report the findings from their own inspection, review, or operational check during the incident review.
shared_context.S6: When a representative identifies an incomplete required control record during the incident review, Elena's routine requires recording a specific closeout commitment for that record before issuing the reopening decision.

PF1.text: Ravi inspected the room after the alarm and found that the sprinkler isolation valve had been left closed during a prior pipe repair; facilities procedure requires reopening the valve and completing a pressure test before the room can be used, and he has not entered the repair closeout yet because the inspection occurred during the active incident response.

PF2.text: Marta's approved next-shift production plan requires exactly 12 battery packs to be charged, and exactly one certified charging attendant is available. Production policy permits that certified attendant to supervise all 12 packs while the required automated monitoring is active. Marta confirmed the schedule and roster with production control this afternoon but has not revised the charging-room work order.

PF3.text: Jonas's post-alarm air test measured hydrogen at 1.2%, above the 1.0% room limit; his compliance procedure requires a 45-minute ventilation purge followed by continuous hydrogen monitoring before charging resumes, and he must both enter an environmental incident record and explicitly cite the 1.2% test result in Elena's reopening plan. He is waiting for the incident review meeting to record the result.

acceptance_conditions: The room must have conditional reopening status and may reopen only after all specified controls are completed.
The sprinkler isolation valve reopening and pressure test must be committed before use.
A facilities repair closeout must be committed.
The room must receive a 45-minute ventilation purge and continuous hydrogen monitoring before charging.
An environmental incident record must be committed.
The 1.2% hydrogen test result must be explicitly cited in the reopening plan.
Exactly 12 battery packs must be authorized with exactly one certified charging attendant.
The hydrogen test finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The closed sprinkler valve and required pressure test change the plan to commit to reopening and testing the valve, while the incomplete repair closeout changes the plan to include a facilities repair closeout commitment.
The approved production plan and exact staffing information change the authorized charging decision to exactly 12 battery packs and exactly one certified attendant.

The measured hydrogen level of 1.2% changes the reopening plan to conditional status with a 45-minute purge and continuous monitoring, while the required incident record and explicit 1.2% citation change the recorded controls and require PF3 to be cited.
